title: A refund on a card the owner issued
narrative: The order is refundable and the support agent has permission, yet the first refund is refused because nobody issued its Refund Card. An owner issues one for REFUND_ORDER, up to €5,000 a day. The next authorization draws €4,000. A second €2,000 proposal is refused while €1,000 remains because that action does not fit. State and authority stay visible as separate checks.

steps.description: An order for €4,000 is paid (state → PAID). Refundable, by the domain's own rules.
The agent proposes the refund holding no card. Refused with no_mandate_issued — nothing wrong with the order, the permission or the state. Nothing has been issued yet.
The owner issues the support agent a Refund Card: REFUND_ORDER, up to €5,000 a day. A person decided; the agent cannot raise it.
The same refund, now authorized against the card. €4,000 is drawn and €1,000 is left for the day — and it is an authorization: your system runs the refund afterwards.

A second €2,000 refund. Refused — not because the card is empty, but because €2,000 does not fit the €1,000 it has left for the day. The order is still refundable and the permission still holds; the authority is what ran short. A smaller refund would still go through, and more room is the owner's decision, which leaves a record.
